name: workflow_run
description:
Execute a workflow by ID after checking workflow_parameters for the workflow's declared input keys.

The workflow starts in a new isolated session and runs in the background unless wait=true. The input object is mapped only to the workflow's parameters node as $input.<name>; top-level run options such as workdir are not workflow input parameters.

Use workdir when a workflow reads/writes files or has bash/tool nodes that must operate in a specific project directory. For directory-specific workflows, workdir may be effectively required by that workflow even though this generic runner keeps it optional for workflows that do not touch the filesystem.

The workflow runner walks the node graph in topological order:
  • parameters nodes  — validate and map the input object onto named workflow parameters ($input.<name>)
  • prompt nodes      — send instructions to the session agent and capture its reply
  • structured nodes  — ask the agent for validated JSON matching the node schema
  • tool nodes        — execute the specified tool with resolved arguments
  • decide nodes      — branch deterministically or ask the agent to choose

Returns the workflow session ID immediately unless wait=true. To check status or read output later, inspect the returned session.

workflowId.description: ID of the workflow to run (use workflow_list to see available IDs)

input.description: Workflow input values keyed by parameters-node name, e.g. {"goal":"...","project_state":"new"}; include every required declared parameter, but do not put top-level runner options such as workdir here.

agentId.description: Agent to use for the workflow session. Defaults to the calling agent. Optional.

workdir.description: Existing working directory for the workflow session and all bash/file-system-sensitive nodes, as an absolute or project-relative path. Pass the exact project directory for existing-project workflows; for new-project workflows, pass an existing parent directory only if the workflow has a separate project/folder-name input that creates the child directory.

wait.description: If true, block until the workflow completes and return its summary. Default: false (fire and forget).
